1.1: And there is a word of Jehovah to Jonah son of Amittai, saying:
1.2: `Rise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim against it that their wickedness has come up before Me.'
1.3: And Jonah rises to flee to Tarshish from the face of Jehovah, and goes down to Joppa, and finds a ship going to Tarshish, and he gives its fare, and goes down into it, to go with them to Tarshish from the face of Jehovah.
1.4: And Jehovah has cast a great wind on the sea, and there is a great tempest in the sea, and the ship has reckoned to be broken;
1.5: and the mariners are afraid, and cry each to his god, and cast the goods that are in the ship into the sea, to make it light of them; and Jonah has gone down to the sides of the vessel, and he lies down, and is fast asleep.
1.6: And the chief of the company draws near to him, and says to him, `What--to you, O sleeper? rise, call to your God, it may be God does bethink himself of us, and we do not perish.'
1.7: And they say each to his neighbour, `Come, and we cast lots, and we know on whose account this evil is on us.' And they cast lots, and the lot falls on Jonah.
1.8: And they say to him, `Declare to us, we pray you, on what account this evil is on us? what is yours occupation, and from where do you come? what is your country, seeing you are not of this people?'
1.9: And he says to them, `A Hebrew I am, and Jehovah, God of the heavens, I am reverencing, who made the sea and the dry land.'
1.10: And the men fear a great fear, and say to him, `What is this you have done!' for the men have known that from the face of Jehovah he is fleeing, for he has told them.
1.11: And they say to him, `What do we do to you that the sea may cease from us, for the sea is more and more tempestuous?'
1.12: And he says to them, `Lift me up, and cast me into the sea, and the sea does cease from you; for I know that on my account this great tempest is upon you.'
1.13: And the men row to turn back to the dry land, and are not able, for the sea is more and more tempestuous against them.
1.14: And they cry to Jehovah, and say, `We pray You, O Jehovah, let us not, we pray You, perish for this man's life, and do not lay on us innocent blood, for You, Jehovah, as You have pleased, You have done.'
1.15: And they lift up Jonah, and cast him into the sea, and the sea ceases from its raging;
1.16: and the men fear Jehovah--a great fear, and sacrifice a sacrifice to Jehovah, and vow vows.
1.17: And Jehovah appoints a great fish to swallow up Jonah, and Jonah is in the bowels of the fish three days and three nights.

2.1: And Jonah prays to Jehovah his God from the bowels of the fish.
2.2: And he says: I called, because of my distress, to Jehovah, And He does answer me, From the belly of sheol I have cried, You have heard my voice.
2.3: When You do cast me into the deep, Into the heart of the seas, Then the flood does compass me, All Your breakers and Your billows have passed over me.
2.4: And I--I said: I have been cast out from before Your eyes, (Yet I add to look to Your holy temple!)
2.5: Compassed me have waters to the soul, The deep does compass me, The weed is bound to my head.
2.6: To the cuttings of mountains I have come down, The earth, her bars are behind me to the age. And You bring up from the pit my life, O Jehovah my God.
2.7: In the feebleness within me of my soul Jehovah I have remembered, And come in to You does my prayer, To Your holy temple.
2.8: Those observing lying vanities their own mercy forsake.
2.9: And I--with a voice of thanksgiving--I sacrifice to You, That which I have vowed I complete, Salvation is of Jehovah.
2.10: And Jehovah says to the fish, and it vomits out Jonah on the dry land.

3.1: And there is a word of Jehovah to Jonah a second time, saying,
3.2: `Rise, go to Nineveh, the great city, and proclaim to it the proclamation that I am speaking to you;'
3.3: and Jonah rises, and he goes to Nineveh, according to the word of Jehovah. And Nineveh has been a great city before God, a journey of three days.
3.4: And Jonah begins to go in to the city a journey of one day, and proclaims, and says, `Yet forty days--and Nineveh is overturned.'
3.5: And the men of Nineveh believe in God, and proclaim a fast, and put on sackcloth, from their greatest even to their least,
3.6: seeing the word does come to the king of Nineveh, and he rises from his throne, and removes his honourable robe from off him, and spreads out sackcloth, and sits on the ashes,
3.7: and he cries and says in Nineveh by a decree of the king and his great ones, saying, `Man and beast, herd and flock--let them not taste anything, let them not feed, even water let them not drink;
3.8: and cover themselves with sackcloth let man and beast, and let them call to God mightily, and let them turn back each from his evil way, and from the violence that is in their hands.
3.9: Who knows? He does turn back, and God has repented, and has turned back from the heat of His anger, and we do not perish.'
3.10: And God sees their works, that they have turned back from their evil way, and God repents of the evil that He spoke of doing to them, and he has not done it.

4.1: And it is grievous to Jonah--a great evil--and he is displeased at it;
4.2: and he prays to Jehovah, and he says, `I pray You, O Jehovah, is not this my word while I was in my own land--therefore I was beforehand to flee to Tarshish--that I have known that You are a God, gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abundant in kindness, and repenting of evil?
4.3: And now, O Jehovah, take, I pray You, my soul from me, for better is my death than my life.'
4.4: And Jehovah says, `Is doing good displeasing to you?'
4.5: And Jonah goes forth from the city, and sits on the east of the city, and makes to himself there a booth, and sits under it in the shade, till that he sees what is in the city.
4.6: And Jehovah God appoints a gourd, and causes it to come up over Jonah, to be a shade over his head, to give deliverance to him from his affliction, and Jonah rejoices because of the gourd with great joy.
4.7: And God appoints a worm at the going up of the dawn on the morrow, and it smites the gourd, and it dries up.
4.8: And it comes to pass, about the rising of the sun, that God appoints a cutting east wind, and the sun smites on the head of Jonah, and he wraps himself up, and asks his soul to die, and says, `Better is my death than my life.'
4.9: And God says to Jonah: `Is doing good displeasing to you, because of the gourd?' and he says, `To do good is displeasing to me--to death.'
4.10: And Jehovah says, `You have had pity on the gourd, for which you did not labour, neither did you nourish it, which a son of a night was, and a son of a night perished,
4.11: and I--have not I pity on Nineveh, the great city, in which there are more than twelve myriads of human beings, who have not known between their right hand and their left--and much cattle!'
